name: claude-push-to-talk
description: Push to talk for the Claude Code extension: sends the message when dictation stops, and reads responses aloud.

claudePushToTalk.globalDictation.markdownDescription:
The dictation key (**Insert** by default) starts dictation anywhere in VS Code (editor, file explorer, Claude panel). **Hold** the key while you speak and release it to stop, or **tap** it once to start and once more to stop (a press shorter than 200 ms is a tap). Focus moves to the Claude input and stays there.

To use a different key, open Keyboard Shortcuts and rebind **Claude Push-to-Talk: Global Dictation Key**.

With the default key this replaces Insert's *overtype mode* function. It does not work in the terminal unless **Dictation In Terminal** is turned on. When turned off, dictation works only in the Claude panel with **Ctrl+D**.

claudePushToTalk.dictationInTerminal.markdownDescription:
Lets the dictation key (**Insert** by default, or the key you assigned) start dictation while the terminal is focused too.

When this is off, the key is passed to the program running in the terminal as usual (for example, `vim` uses Insert to switch between insert and replace mode). When it is on, programs in the terminal no longer receive that key.

claudePushToTalk.autoSubmit.markdownDescription: Submits the message automatically when dictation stops: when you release the dictation key after holding it, or tap it a second time (**Insert** by default, or **Ctrl+D** in the Claude panel). When turned off, the text stays in the input box and you have to press Enter.

claudePushToTalk.submitDelayMs.markdownDescription: How long to wait, in milliseconds, after dictation stops before the message is submitted. The last words reach the input box a moment after you stop speaking, so the message cannot be sent instantly: values below `300` are treated as `300`. Increase it if the last words are being cut off.

claudePushToTalk.clearOnCancel.markdownDescription:
Press **Esc** while dictating to cancel: dictation stops and the message is not sent.

When this is on, the input box is also emptied after a cancel. This removes everything in the box, including any text you typed before dictating. When it is off, the dictated text stays in the box.

claudePushToTalk.readAloud.markdownDescription:
Reads the text aloud when Claude finishes a response. This needs a selected voice; see **Voice**. You can also toggle it with **Claude Push-to-Talk: Toggle Read Aloud** from the Command Palette.

To stop the current reading, press the stop-speaking key (**Alt+X** by default). To use a different key, open Keyboard Shortcuts and rebind **Claude Push-to-Talk: Stop Speaking**.

claudePushToTalk.voice.markdownDescription:
The voice that reads responses. It reads every text, whatever its language; the voice is not picked by language.

**[Select a voice](command:claudePushToTalk.pickVoice)** to choose from the voices on this computer (**Claude Push-to-Talk: Select Read-Aloud Voice** in the Command Palette). That list is also where you download a Piper voice, install a Windows voice or remove downloaded voices. This field shows the name of the selected voice.

No voice is selected at first, and nothing is read until you select one; the extension asks the first time it starts. On **Windows** you can use the voices installed in Windows or download [Piper](https://github.com/rhasspy/piper) voices; on **Linux**, which has no built-in voices, Piper voices are the only kind. Piper voices run on this computer (the first download is about 90 MB, each further voice about 60 MB).

claudePushToTalk.rate.markdownDescription: Reading speed. `1.0` is normal speed; `1.5` is noticeably fast.

claudePushToTalk.maxChars.markdownDescription: The maximum number of characters to read from a response. Set it to `0` to read the whole response.
